title: pint: don't define inline functions twice.
description:
That prevents having different definitions with different function
signatures, which led to bug #21455.

The one such error was fixed in !25994, but this makes perhaps a bit
cleaner.

Also, do some rework of the comments.

Undefine the internal macros so that they're not exported from the
header.

AI-Assisted: no

This looks easier to read and less likely to lead to mistakes IMO.

A little bit of testing with godbolt.org shows that gcc and clang still don't seem to optimize anything other than the 16, 32, and 64-bit versions very much, though clang will divide up a little-endian 56-bit load into "32 + 16 + 8" (gcc does not, and does 7 separate byte loads.)

> though clang will divide up a little-endian 56-bit load into "32 + 16 + 8"

That's the sort of optimizing I was thinking of.

> (gcc does not, and does 7 separate byte loads.)

Hopefully the GCC and Clang/LLVM developers are following what each other are doing here.

> This looks easier to read and less likely to lead to mistakes IMO.

Or, at least, it buries most of the Twisty Little Maze Of Ifdefs, All Different in the macro definitions.

commits_data.title: pint: don't define inline functions twice.
commits_data.message:
pint: don't define inline functions twice.

That prevents having different definitions with different function
signatures, which led to bug #21455.

The one such error was fixed in !25994, but this makes perhaps a bit
cleaner.

Also, do some rework of the comments.

Undefine the internal macros so that they're not exported from the
header.
